lines.cap: The Moon is slowly pulling out.
lines.say: The Moon is slowly pulling out.

lines.cap: Every year, it moves about 3.8 centimetres further away from Earth.
lines.say: Every year, it moves about 3.8 centimetres further away from Earth.

lines.cap: We know because Apollo astronauts left mirrors on the Moon. Scientists bounce lasers off them, and time the light.
lines.say: We know because Apollo astronauts left mirrors on the Moon. Scientists bounce lasers off them, and time the light.

lines.cap: The cause? The tides. The Moon pulls on Earth's oceans, and the bulge of water pulls the Moon forward, into a bigger orbit.
lines.say: The cause? The tides. The Moon pulls on Earth's oceans, and the bulge of water pulls the Moon forward, into a bigger orbit.

lines.cap: Meanwhile, Earth slows down. Days are getting longer, by a tiny bit every century.
lines.say: Meanwhile, Earth slows down. Days are getting longer, by a tiny bit every century.

lines.cap: Hundreds of millions of years ago, a day on Earth was much shorter.
lines.say: Hundreds of millions of years ago, a day on Earth was much shorter.

lines.cap: One day, far in the future, the Moon will look too small to cover the Sun. No more total eclipses.
lines.say: One day, far in the future, the Moon will look too small to cover the Sun. No more total eclipses.

lines.cap: So enjoy the view. It's slowly pulling out.
lines.say: So enjoy the view. It's slowly pulling out.
